# Mathematics fundamentals and resources

## Why This Matters

Mathematics is the language behind models, optimization, and algorithmic thinking in bioinformatics.

## Learning Outcomes

- Use vectors and matrices to reason about high-dimensional data.
- Understand derivatives/integrals for optimization and rates of change.
- Apply discrete math and algorithms in sequence and graph problems.
- Recognize when numerical methods are needed for approximations.

## Suggested Time

- **Minimum**: 2 weeks (focused review)
- **Recommended**: 3-4 weeks (with exercises)

## Key Concepts
- Linear Algebra: Vectors, matrices, and their applications
- Calculus: Differential and integral calculus
- Discrete Mathematics: Combinatorics, graph theory
- Algorithms and Data Structures
- Numerical Methods

## Recommended Resources
- **Books**:
  - *Introduction to Linear Algebra* by Gilbert Strang
  - *Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications* by Kenneth H. Rosen
  - *Numerical Recipes* by William H. Press et al.

- **Online Courses**:
  - [Linear Algebra](https://www.edx.org/course/linear-algebra-foundations-to-frontiers) on edX
  - [Calculus 1A: Differentiation](https://www.edx.org/course/calculus-1a-differentiation) on edX
